title: Hawaii Leads US in Life Expectancy
paragraphs: We often talk about life expectancies on a country-by-country basis. However, people living in the same country can expect very different lifespans depending on where exactly they live.
And according to 2022 data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Hawaii is the US state with the highest life expectancy, at 80 years.
This is close to eight years higher than the US state with the lowest life expectancy — West Virginia, which has a life expectancy of 72.2 years.
2022 is the most recent year for which data is available.
The US state with the second-highest life expectancy is Massachusetts, at 79.8 years. The third highest is New Jersey, at 79.6 years.

Meanwhile, the state with the second-lowest average lifespan after West Virginia is Mississippi, where life expectancy is 72.6 years. Just ahead of Mississippi is Kentucky at 73.6 years — one whole year longer.
The reasons for these very different life expectancies have been studied separately by researchers from Yale University, who looked at more than 179 million US deaths between 1969 and 2020.
They found that issues like poverty, having less access to healthcare and poorer public health programs all negatively affect state life expectancies.
Average life expectancy for the whole US in 2022 was 77.5, which increased to 80.2 for women and fell to 74.8 for men.
That gender split can be seen state-by-state too, meaning Hawaiian women have the country's highest life expectancy at 83 years, compared with 77.1 years for men.
In fact, men in Massachusetts have an average longer life than Hawaiian men, at 77.4 years. Women in Massachusetts have a life expectancy of 82.2.
In West Virginia, women's life expectancy is above the state average, at 75.1. But among men it falls to just 69.5.
